exclusions.description: Signed-channel publication and promotion require protected CI environments and release credentials.
Replacing or restarting a review broker is a separate ownership-aware deployment action.
Linux ARM64, Android, macOS, iOS, and Windows builds require their declared CI runners.
Physical-device, multi-host, reboot, and real-agent evidence is never inferred from deterministic fixtures.

claims.description: The release verification inventory is complete, resolvable, and uniquely owned.
The implementation has no whitespace errors.
Workflow runners, permissions, paths, graph use, and action pins are valid.
The public-source boundary has no findings: every tracked path, text body, and binary is reviewed.
The public-source boundary gate still enforces every personal, private-network, and internal-documentation rule.
Package dependency directions, adapter isolation, and Flutter platform boundaries pass without findings.
Generated contract artifacts match the immutable current revision.
Published contract revision and hash history is append-only.
Tool capability discovery and fixtures remain truthful.
Trace evidence manifests are structurally valid.
Adapter support claims retain evidence coverage.
The release source graph typechecks.
Canonical messages and registered adapters conform.
Routes, error codes, frames, and client messages do not drift.

The aggregated usage report projects Tokdash by explicit field selection: prompt text never reaches the DTO, the period total travels beside the facet rows, an older Tokdash degrades to a report without facets, and windows are cached per range.
Codex reviewer state and native permission modes survive resume.
CLI, first-run, cleanup, signals, and packaged process boundaries hold.
Compiled runtime assets and packaged hook exclusions are correct.
The cosyncing application and the runtime executing it stay distinct across every acquisition path.
The npm distribution is one JavaScript package with no embedded runtime and no platform packages.
Same-origin web serving: the /cosy/ mount, the retired /app path, and no route shadowing.
Durable state, credentials, migration, and Pi route scope stay isolated.

Zero-agent diagnosis, isolated paths, and topology checks remain deterministic, and doctor resolves a managed host's identity under the USER home while reading receipts and ownership records from cosyncing's STATE home — collapsing the two names a host nothing uses, which silently reads as unmanaged and hands back the manual start command.
Setup re-entry, rollback, occupied-port, and legacy-discovery behavior is transactional.
Service ownership, restart, lingering, rollback, and WSL fixtures pass.
Provider-neutral one-time pairing and revocation remain safe.
Repair, upgrade, rollback, uninstall, and retention state machines pass.
OpenCode shim installation and removal stay symmetric.
OpenCode shim routing and fallback behavior pass.
Roster revisions, ETags, deltas, and reconnect resets remain deterministic.

Roster discovery is bounded in work and in time: every adapter applies the cutoff before expensive native decoding, and no single backend can hold the roster — a backend whose discovery crosses to a host the broker does not own declares a budget, and a host that accepts connections and never answers is abandoned and cancelled at that budget while the established agents' rows still come back, whether or not that backend honours its abort.

The broker starts or stops an external agent host ONLY when it can prove it started that exact process — pid, a start token that survives pid reuse, the boot it started in, and the address the record was written for must all match — and re-proves it immediately before every signal, so a pid recycled between deciding and acting is never signalled; a serving host, an occupied-but-unready address, an unidentifiable process, and a damaged ownership record are all preserved untouched, and a spawned child whose own identity cannot be read is stopped again rather than leaked as a process no later broker could ever prove it owns. Proof is scoped to one BOOT, because a Linux start token counts ticks since boot and would otherwise let a post-reboot stranger inherit a pid and start token; a missing command name makes the process lookup indeterminate, but a changed non-empty name does not revoke otherwise matching proof because a process can rename itself at runtime. "Nothing is there" and "this machine will not say" are never the same answer: only a proven-empty address is spawned into, only a proven-gone process has its record cleared, and a failed stop keeps the proof that authorizes the next attempt. A start reconciles the RECORD independently of the address, so a host that released its listener but still runs — or one left behind by a repointed configuration, including a repoint onto an address somebody else already serves — is settled rather than kept alive until shutdown or having its only proof overwritten; that reconciliation reaps nothing it cannot prove is a DIFFERENT process from the one holding the address, so an unnameable address and our own serving host are both left strictly alone. A descriptor that cannot launch is not a shortcut around any of that: moving a managed host to a remote or operator-run one reaps the local process we started rather than leaving it alive until shutdown. No outcome that ends without a running host is silent, and silence is not reachable by accident: what to say is decided next to the outcome type, exhaustively, so an unhandled variant fails to compile rather than reaching an operator as nothing. A start blocked by a predecessor, a host of ours still running that nothing can now reap, and an address held by something unready that is not ours or cannot be identified all reach the operator pointed at doctor — built from our own closed vocabulary, never from another program's output, and never claiming a host is somebody else's when the honest answer is that we could not tell. Release reads that record as its primary input, so a host stays reapable even when the adapter stops describing it, which is exactly when a second host has appeared. Readiness proves the serving process IS the spawned child before ownership is claimed, and the advertised deadline bounds the wait for an answer rather than the interval between questions — measured from the spawn, so a hung pre-flight probe or a slow reap cannot spend a fresh host's budget and then fail it for being slow. Supervision restarts only a host proven crashed or proven ours-and-wedged, under a crash-loop budget, and shutdown waits for a recovery already in flight before releasing. Uninstall stops only a still-proven owned child and reports every other host as preserved.
Real control loss emits and recovers degradation without false positives.
Live status, prompt identity, footer, and pageable replay stay coherent.
Adapter watcher snapshots are owner-qualified before any roster revision; an exact live turn never journals an inferred Idle reversal.
Capability-driven model catalogs reach immediate and scheduled creation.
Managed, restarted, absent, and external agent runtimes expose bounded truthful create readiness.
Pi creation qualifies its executable identity and effective Node runtime without blocking setup.
Oversized diffs become bounded, signed, durable references.
WebSocket diff references serve the exact full body.
OpenCode diffs map to canonical per-file changes.
OpenCode retry detail remains bounded and control-free.
Client prompt correlation is exact and ambiguity-safe.
Drive restoration and takeover arbitration stay single-owner-safe.
Pending requests resolve exactly once and ignore orphans.
Notification bulk clear remains bounded, durable, and revision-safe.
Agent-owned sessions reject user forks with a typed result.
Composer drafts fan out and clear on accepted send.
Draft revisions, tombstones, and sender-owned clear survive restart.
Two clients arbitrate draft revisions and stale writes correctly.
Idempotency replays terminal mutation outcomes across restart.
All native history mappers stay within named cache and cursor bounds.
WebSocket paging reuses immutable snapshots across clients and restart.
Resync snapshots are authoritative resets serialized with live delivery.
Persisted-final/live-buffer overlap keeps one message identity.
Logical messages keep identity across broker restart.
Codex rollout replay and live delivery share exact identities.

Session identity, run-state authority, terminal exactly-once, and canonical chronology are invariant across attach, watcher, replay, reconnect, replacement, and interleaved delivery for main and subagent sessions.
The Codex watcher publishes derived rows only on real transitions and serializes async scans.
A failed Codex loaded-thread probe is unknown evidence and never fabricates Idle.
Codex terminal presence qualifies sync and control state without misattributing ownership.
The bounded Codex TUI presence scan degrades to explicit unknowns, never to false attribution.
The per-agent Codex sync enabler persists durably and applies at construction without restart.
Claude transcript replay and live delivery share exact identities.

A prompt driven into a Claude session is published by the adapter as a keyed pending row the moment it is accepted (queued only when a turn was already running), replayed from history until the transcript line delivers it under the SAME key on both the live tail and the replay, never minted for a slash command, left honestly queued when the CLI drops it, and refused before any run state changes when no child process exists.

Claude subagent transcripts reach the roster as observe-only CHILD rows of the session that spawned them, and never as sessions of their own: a child carries origin 'subagent' and the parent's published nativeId (the bridge id where the parent has one), a childless parent invents no native identity, and only a parent-spawned `subagents/agent-*.meta.json` carrying a toolUseId becomes a row — workflow-owned metas, meta-less transcripts, and the nested `subagents/workflows/<run>/` agents stay out, because they are already summarized inside their workflow's activity card. A child id is base64url of its own path, so attach's realpath containment admits it unchanged while a path outside every projects root is still refused, and its connection replays the CHILD transcript rather than the parent's. Observe-only is enforced rather than advertised: a child offers no Drive, no take-over, and no terminal command that cannot work, and a driving attach on one is refused before any process path. Discovery stays bounded — a parent outside the roster cutoff contributes no children, because its tree is never walked.

A Claude roster row is dated and statused by real conversation evidence, never by sidecar churn. `updatedAt` comes from the last timestamped conversation line, so a `permission-mode` or `bridge-session` rewrite that only bumps mtime cannot make a stale session look fresh. Status projection is layered: exact terminal turn authority settles Idle; exact active authority is qualified by the live `agents --json` row rather than by recency; and only a transcript with NO exact latest-turn marker falls through to the freshness gate, where a raw busy row backed by nothing newer than an old conversation event reads Idle instead of a wedged Working. A parent-launched background Task that is still unnotified keeps the row Working for its pending window even though `agents --json` reports nothing — the spawning tool_use line is itself an exact active marker, so this upgrade must apply to an active turn the live row leaves idle or the fallback is unreachable for every real transcript. It never outranks live busy or needs-input evidence. Fork transcripts sharing a first user turn carry that turn's uuid as a common lineageId, and the current model is the transcript TAIL model with the adapter-authored tier label the roster reads — a wrapper's unknown model carries no invented label.
OpenCode live/history identity is stable without equal-text dedupe.
OpenCode completion follows authoritative idle/error and notification fences.

The Kimi adapter's write surface is CLOSED by construction: the shared HTTP door is GET-only, the single write door exposes exactly ten named POST operations with no generic post and no escape hatch, no other adapter source names a mutating HTTP verb, its socket sends only allowlisted read-only frames, every server it reads is identity-verified or refused, and every untrusted string it turns into a filesystem path must be one safe component resolving under the Kimi home.
Kimi native payloads map totally into canonical rows, degrading unknown roles and content instead of misattributing them, under stable per-part identities.
Kimi read-only observe surfaces terminal-driven turns through a bounded pull refresh and reports incomplete history honestly.

Kimi Drive is reachable only for sessions cosyncing created: a foreign session refuses a live attach, a live attach whose safety stream never opens refuses rather than degrading to poll-only, every content write requires that stream at write time (the abort alone is exempt) and goes through the enumerated write door of the CURRENT transport generation, a user prompt seen while the stream was down is held rather than recorded as accounted for, and a proven foreign writer demotes the connection to observe before another write lands. PROVEN means silence across POLLS, and only a poll is one: a reconnect fires several unawaited refreshes in close succession — the tick, the re-verification finishing, a restored stream adopting its cursor, a frame saying the transcript moved — and a read is not an interval, so no number of them can confirm a suspect the server was about to account for. The next poll still confirms it, unchanged.

Kimi doctor applies the adapter identity gate and treats an off-PATH install as installed; production doctor diagnoses Kimi unconditionally, from the same shipped-adapter list the installed service derives managed-host activation from, so an agent can never be diagnosed in one and left unmanaged in the other. What a diagnosis tells an operator to DO follows the machine's posture rather than the agent's name. Where cosyncing is responsible for the host, NO remediation names the tool's own command — not the start, not the restarts, not the instruction to reduce several servers to one — because stopping a supervised host opens the window its supervisor fills, so a manual restart ends in two servers exactly as a manual start does. The posture is scoped to a CONFIGURATION rather than to the agent: the broker reports which host identities it manages — the home the service's own environment resolves, and the home an ownership record was written for — and a diagnosis applies the managed wording only to the home it actually resolved, so an operator whose shell names another `KIMI_CODE_HOME` is never told that a host nothing supervises is supervised. The posture is proven by a committed durable-service receipt OR by an ownership record that still identifies a process, and each covers what the other cannot: a first startup has no record to find, a foreground broker has no service, and a record whose process is proven gone manages nothing and must not silence the instructions an unmanaged operator needs. The receipt is read as a receipt: managed hosts are default-on in the environment setup writes and that file is not a live opt-out, so a missing, unreadable, or drifted environment — one switched explicitly off included — cannot withdraw what a running service already loaded. The managed wording claims only that cosyncing is CONFIGURED to manage the host, never that it owns the process answering right now, which may be the operator's own. Only the remediation differs between postures; status, detail code, and evidence are identical. Setup LISTS Kimi in its installable-agent summary, and names the `kimi web` host in the managed-runtime consent it shows before writing that activation: the service it installs starts, restarts, and stops that host, so a host absent from the disclosure would be one managed without being disclosed.
A Kimi attach withholds live rows until history primes the connection, so no row is delivered both live and in the reset.

Kimi subagent journals reach the roster as observe-only CHILD rows of the session that spawned them, never as sessions of their own. Enumeration is authored by `state.json`'s `agents` map rather than by the directory listing: its `type` is the discriminant, `main` is never a child, a reused slot takes the title of its NEWEST spawn record, and a directory the map does not list yields no row. Lineage holds on rows the real discovery path built — `child.parentThreadId === parent.nativeId` — and a CHILDLESS parent publishes no `nativeId` at all, so no identity is invented store-wide for parents that never spawned anything. Discovery stays bounded: children spend from the sweep's own row ceiling, the cutoff filters on the CHILD's own mtime, and every ceiling reached is reported rather than silently applied. Observe-only is ENFORCED, not merely advertised — a non-observe attach is refused before any transport is touched and every mutation on the connection rejects — and a child's attach replays the CHILD's own journal through the measured mapper, where an unknown line type renders nothing plus a trace instead of a guessed card, and the user row is never duplicated.

Kimi Drive authority is socket-local and never inferred: a background no-mode attach on an owned session gets no mutation authority and issues no write, an explicit mode=live attach is a distinct Hub owner that can drive, and no bare attach folding onto the shared key ever inherits authority from it.

Two sockets share ONE Claude Drive connection through the broker's join action, which is what a page reload depends on: a bare attach while this broker's own `claude -p --resume` owner is driving gets a different, read-only observe connection whose history is the transcript alone (so an accepted, still-undelivered prompt is absent from it), is offered joinExisting, and the join reuses the exact owner with no native attach — one writer, one child — and replays the owner's pending driven row; a socket that suppressed the action or declared itself read-only is never offered the join or granted authority, and a stale owner revision fails closed.

Two cosyncing clients share ONE Kimi Drive connection through the broker's join action: the second socket is offered joinExisting in either attach order (observe after drive, or drive taken while an observer is already open, which reaches it as a pushed session frame with no re-attach), the join reuses the exact owner with no native attach so the session keeps a single writer, a stale owner revision fails closed, and a socket that suppressed the action or declared itself read-only is never offered the join or granted authority.

A broker that cannot start exits non-zero and promptly through both entry points, keeping its diagnostic and leaving no surviving child or listener; the shared fixture starter respawns a broker that lost a port race onto a fresh port, while any other startup failure is reported rather than retried.

One visibility decision covers EVERY roster read — the agent list, the session snapshot, the delta stream that updates it, the aggregated machine roster, and the resolution that turns one of its rows into an owning broker — because an agent hidden as undecodable while its sessions still arrive is worse than no filtering at all, and a row a client can SEE must be a row it can open rather than a 404, and a broker asks its peers as the current client it is rather than as the oldest possible one. Kimi is registered for every broker and shown only to clients that can decode its row: a client declaring nothing, one below the integration-kind tolerance, or one whose revision is not a canonical decimal integer is served no Kimi row and keeps every other agent, while a client at or above that tolerance is served it — and every attach mode the row publishes predates the later attach-mode tolerance, so the declared floor is honest rather than merely safe. The served row carries the whole surface — observe first, live attach, model switching, and a wired create hook — because the Drive rollout gate is gone: a flag nobody was expected to set meant the surface most users would meet was the one that never shipped, and ownership plus the requested attach mode, enforced per session, is what actually keeps a write safe. A machine with no host running refuses a create as TEMPORARY and retryable, naming the command that fixes it, rather than as a permanent claim that the tool cannot create sessions. The durable service environment carries no rollout gate and no retired one, and does carry managed-host activation for every agent that declares an external host — derived from the adapters rather than from a list of tool names — because an installed service that can see a host but never start, recover, or stop one is the same as the agent not working. Setup LISTS the row in its installable-agent summary and names `kimi web` in the managed-runtime consent, from the same declaration that activates it, so the runtimes an operator agrees to are the runtimes cosyncing manages.

The dsh transport surface is closed by construction: exactly the round-1 unary methods plus respond and the two stream routes are reachable, every deferred method and traversal variant is refused, path building lives in one source file, the unary envelope fails closed on a mismatched rpcId, a foreign envelope, a non-200, or a body past the ceiling (abandoned mid-stream), and the two push-only downlinks form ONE generation whose frames reach no session until host.describe validates — a failed probe discards them, and a superseded connection's close cannot evict its replacement.

dsh native events fold totally into canonical rows without enumerating plugins: a real captured turn maps exactly, an unrecognized event type becomes an honest activity record instead of a throw or a silent drop, tool cards come only from the host-computed view with the documented generic JSON fallback, and the projection store is generic higher-seq-wins seeded from the history tail's consistent cut, keeping unknown keys readable but never forwarding raw dsh-shaped values.

A dsh attach withholds live transcript until history primes it and admits each event exactly once through one seq gate across the buffered, cap-breach, timeout and post-reconnect paths; a subscribe whose tail is ahead proves a gap and one behind proves a restarted host, both re-baselining wholesale and rewinding the gate so reused sequence numbers read as new content; pending prompts converge across clients rather than stranding a card another client answered; and removal is terminal for authority, mutation, and transient frames while a durable transcript event still arrives exactly once.

Every dsh write is the host's own contract or refuses: prompts post their queue/steer placement, answers echo the asking rpcId and re-attach selections to their native ids, a single-select answer carries at most one of selected/custom, an app-sent prompt's minted rpcId converges its own echo without claiming another client's message, a bad-response receipt throws and keeps the card while not-pending settles it as resolved elsewhere, unimplemented seams are absent rather than throwing stubs, and an attachment is refused outright instead of being sent as text naming a file the agent never received.

dsh doctor says only what a read-only, effect-free observer can prove, and what it tells an operator to DO follows the same posture rule as every other managed host: where cosyncing manages this one, an absent host yields no `dsh web` command at all, because instructing a manual start while the service is starting or recovering one leaves two hosts on a single address. The posture is scoped by ADDRESS rather than by agent: the managed wording applies only to an address the broker reports managing, so a host on another machine is never described as supervised. That address also decides the command, and a non-default one never receives `dsh web` at all — managed or not — because that command takes no address and would start a host at the default one instead: not the host being diagnosed, and precisely the address a service manages. The operator is told which address to start instead. Beyond that, it opens no socket and issues no RPC of its own, separates "a server is listening" from "a dsh host is listening" by the upgrade-required downlink fingerprint, treats an npx cache with no binary on PATH as an advisory rather than an install, fails a build below the exact tested floor, and refuses a non-http(s) or query-bearing base URL instead of probing it — redacting any credential rather than quoting the configured value.

Driven through the real adapter registry and a real Hub, owner keying included. A dsh session has exactly ONE owner and only by explicit request: bare, observe and resume attaches are all refused and leave no owner, an explicit live attach is the sole owner on the #live key, a bare attach arriving AFTER it is still refused so no second full-authority owner can take over frame routing, and a repeated live attach coalesces onto the same wrapper and connection — two clients share it, and one disconnecting neither replaces routing nor silences the other. On that owner: live rows are withheld until history primes, so the history/live overlap reaches every client exactly once; both re-baseline signals arrive as a wholesale history re-read — a reconnect gap with its notice, and a proven host restart that retracts the previous generation to a shorter thread and then admits its reused sequence numbers as new content. Removal retracts Drive authority and the running state to the Hub, refuses later mutations, drops late transient frames while a durable transcript event emitted before it still arrives, and does not disturb another attached session.

A downlink generation rotating underneath an in-flight session create must not report the host as unavailable. The create path shares one unary client with the downlinks, and the abort that ends an epoch used to take every in-flight call with it, including the calls that decide creatability. The host parks one chosen method on a gate so the rotation lands while that exact call is on the wire, and each surviving call is covered by its OWN case rather than by a case that holds several and rotates on the first: the readiness host.describe, the readiness workspace.list, requireVerifiedHost's own host.describe, and the session.create write. Removing any single policy marker turns exactly one case red. A session-scoped session.list is STILL aborted by the generation it belongs to, so the abort is scoped rather than removed, and the rotation names itself and its reason in the log instead of taking an unrelated call down silently. A final case reproduces the reported sequence end to end rather than by forcing a socket close: a session is created, the attach that follows opens a generation whose verification is still outstanding, the host bursts one frame past the pre-verification cap so the generation dies of its own documented overflow condition, and the second create issued in that window still returns a distinct session.

The attachment path an ordinary screenshot takes, driven through the REAL upload store rather than a stand-in. The first-party client stages every attachment as a file and switches to a chunked upload above the inline ceiling, so the interesting image arrives by staged reference: completing one moves it into the session inbox and rewrites the record, and the adapter then delivers a 400 KiB image to session.prompt exactly once with its bytes intact. Refusals are decided before any byte is read and name the real cause: a type the host has no route for is refused on its type, and an image past the host's own per-image bound is refused from its size on disk rather than after a multi-megabyte read.

dsh is registered for every broker and shown only to clients that can decode its row: a client declaring nothing, one below the integration-kind tolerance, or one whose revision is not a canonical decimal integer is served no dsh row and keeps every other agent, while a client at or above that tolerance is served exactly one — and its only attach mode predates the later attach-mode tolerance, so the declared floor is honest. The served row is honestly live-only: http-websocket, no observe and no resume (both refused rather than silently downgraded), the reviewed per-tool Drive posture, native rename as its only write-class action, and a typed retryable refusal when no external host is reachable. The host ADDRESS never becomes durable service state — pointing the adapter elsewhere is a foreground decision, and a remote address is not this machine's to serve — while managed-host ACTIVATION is durable and on by default, so the installed service starts and stops a locally launchable host it owns. Setup LISTS the row in its installable-agent summary and names `dsh web` in the managed-runtime consent, from the same declaration that activates it, so the runtimes an operator agrees to are the runtimes cosyncing manages.

The Antigravity CLI store is read WITHOUT being written to: the summaries database opens read-only and leaves no WAL or shm sidecar behind, `app_data_dir` is filtered in SQL at the boundary so an IDE row — whose per-conversation store is an opaque container this build deliberately does not support — can never reach the roster, a conversation with a store and NO transcript still yields an honest row whose history is a stated notice rather than an empty session, the discovery cutoff and the per-sweep row budget are both honoured, and a conversation id that would escape the app-data root is refused instead of addressing a path. The zero-time sentinel every summary row carries is matched textually before any parse, because `Date.parse` reads it as a plausible date rather than as nothing and would misdate the entire roster.

The measured `(source, type)` inventory folds TOTALLY, keyed on the pair and never on the type alone: all sixteen measured pairs land in the category the table states, and an unlisted pair becomes a NAMED NEUTRAL row carrying its own source and type plus a trace — never a user bubble, never a throw. `USER_EXPLICIT/USER_INPUT` is the only human bubble, and the harness's own wrappers are stripped off it so the app never renders text the user did not type. Tool rows carry their semantic and their exit code, `CONVERSATION_HISTORY` is a history reset, and a background-task settlement is a self-contained tool block keyed by its sender and joined to the step index that spawned it — a result that finds no pending call becomes a self-contained block plus a trace rather than a guessed correlation to an unrelated call.

An observe attach replays a recorded conversation and then tails the same file, admitting each step EXACTLY ONCE across the buffered, cutoff and re-read paths — the byte offset bounds the read and the admitted-step set is the identity fence, so a debounced double-fire or a drain racing a replay still cannot emit a step twice. A transcript that SHRINKS was rewritten rather than appended to, so it re-baselines wholesale and tells every client to reload instead of splicing two different transcripts together. A `RUNNING` row replayed with no live child reads as interrupted, never as running. Removal is terminal for transient frames while a durable row emitted before it still arrives.

Every Antigravity write is the host's own contract or it refuses. A prompt MINTS its own pending row before the child admits it — agy records nothing that could correlate until it writes the transcript line, so without this a refresh would delete the user's words — and that row survives a `getHistory()` replay, which is the only thing an ordinary attach reads. The delivering transcript line CLAIMS the row's key rather than minting a second, fenced by the transcript's byte size at send time so a repeated identical prompt cannot claim a line written before its send; rows and their correlation links are bounded together, so an evicted row leaves no link behind to lend its key to a later repeat. A send against a dead or never-spawned child REJECTS before touching run state rather than vanishing under a Running badge, a stream that closes owing a `result` is surfaced as a failure instead of hanging forever on the measured exit-0 trap, exit codes are traced and never interpreted, and a foreign `USER_EXPLICIT` line self-demotes the connection without killing the tail — a demotion keeps the accepted prompts and only `close()` drops them.

Live and replay agree KEY FOR KEY: one recorded fixture driven through both paths produces identical keys in identical order, which is what makes `mapAgyStep()` one fold rather than two that resemble each other — the stream names steps in lower snake case and the file in upper, and `agent_response` ↔ `PLANNER_RESPONSE` is not a case fold, so the normalization table at the boundary is what the agreement rests on. The drive registry is IDENTITY-KEYED and compare-and-swap: the hub can attach a replacement before closing the incumbent it displaced, so a stale close cannot deregister its live replacement and leave the session driving while every roster row reads observing.

agy is registered for EVERY broker — on the runtime registry that serves `/api/agents` and on the shipped-adapter list doctor diagnoses, which must never disagree — and served to every client that can decode its row, which is all of them: a client declaring nothing, one below either decode tolerance, and one whose revision is not a canonical decimal integer are all served exactly one agy row and keep every other agent. That absence of a declared floor is proved rather than assumed — every attach mode it publishes predates the attach-mode tolerance and its integration kind predates the integration-kind one, so a later value added without a floor fails here instead of costing an old client its whole roster. The DECLARED attach modes and the modes `attach` honours are the same set, and an undeclared mode is refused loudly rather than silently downgraded. An observe attach spawns NO child, observed through a fake binary that records its own argv, and a bare attach is observe — never silently promoted to a drive, with no driver registered and its writes refused outright. A resume attach claims the session and still spawns nothing until the first prompt, while a machine with no `agy` on PATH refuses the resume as an ordinary attach refusal and leaves no half-built drive registered behind it. There is no managed host in the durable service environment, because there is no daemon to start, supervise or stop.

Two sockets share ONE Antigravity Drive connection through the broker's join action. The second socket is OFFERED the join — a capability that stays silent is never offered it, which was the whole of two shipped defects — receives the EXISTING connection rather than a second child, and sees the owner's accepted-but-undelivered prompts in its own REPLAY, which is the row a reload used to lose. The join performs no native attach and spawns no second process, so the conversation still has exactly one writer against one stdin: both sockets' prompts arrive there in order, each as the measured `{"event":"user"}` envelope, and a peer socket's prompt is never mistaken for a foreign write because the pending FIFO and the queued-key map live on the CONNECTION they share. A foreign write in a terminal demotes that connection and the new posture reaches BOTH sockets in the same broadcast, retracting authority from both at once, offering a takeover rather than pretending the session is unreachable, keeping every accepted prompt, and refusing later sends instead of racing the terminal.
Loopback auth, Observe, direct resume, Pi scope, and corruption boundaries hold.

Artifact creation, replay, restart, and download stay bound to one exact broker, tool, and session. An artifact download is resumable on the same terms as the workspace route: it advertises `accept-ranges`, carries the record's content hash as its ETag and its creation time as `last-modified`, answers the closed, open, and suffix byte-range forms exactly, honours a matching `If-Range` with a 206 and a stale one with the whole representation, refuses a range outside the representation with 416 and `content-range: bytes */size`, and answers a ranged `HEAD` with those headers and no body. Two half ranges concatenate to the artifact byte-for-byte. Every security header on the 200 — `nosniff`, `content-disposition`, `content-security-policy: sandbox` for a non-passive mime, `no-store`, the referrer and cross-origin policies — is identical on the 206 and on the 416, so no range can turn a hardened attachment into an inline-renderable response.

A prompt attachment reaches its agent through one bounded, identity-bound intake. A chunked upload initializes, resumes from the offset the broker recorded, and completes byte-exact into the session inbox even when the file is larger than the legacy 32 MB WebSocket frame cap, falling back to copy+unlink when the rename crosses a filesystem; upload ids are broker-issued UUIDs that cannot escape the staging root, oversized init bodies, chunks, and PATCH bodies are refused with stable codes before anything is written, and the routes require auth wherever a token is configured. The older `images` route is bounded to the same ceilings as inline files rather than forwarded verbatim: a non-array field, a non-canonical or `data:`-prefixed payload, a missing mimeType, and a client-asserted broker path are each refused, count, per-image decoded bytes and aggregate encoded bytes are bounded, and an adapter that declares no native file input is never handed images at all. A completed upload yields an opaque staged reference and never a filesystem path: only the prompt that owns it can claim it, another client profile or incarnation cannot, a consumed reference cannot be replayed outside journal dedupe, and rollback releases it again for retry while removing the inline files it materialized. Inline and staged files keep prompt order and exact bytes, the adapter handoff carries broker paths but no inline bytes and no staged secret, client-supplied filesystem paths are refused, attachment count, per-file inline bytes, and aggregate inline bytes are each bounded, an expiry sweep never takes an upload whose completion hashing is still running, and expired staging is rejected and cleaned.

Delivered prompt attachments are collected from the session inbox under a bounded age, byte, and count policy, and a file a live session may still reference is never removed. A delivered inline or staged attachment past the retention age goes whatever else is in the inbox; over either per-inbox cap the oldest go first and eviction stops at the retained-file floor, which bounds the caps and never the age. Four things are never removed: anything that is not a regular file, so a symlink inside the inbox is neither followed nor deleted; a path an unexpired or claimed staging record still points at; anything inside the grace window while a live session holds that cwd; and every file under a `.cosyncing` that no longer resolves to itself, which is refused outright rather than swept. The sweep is durable and bounded — session cwds are registered as they are used and survive a restart, a directory that is gone is dropped from the registry, and one call inspects a bounded number of roots and advances a persisted round-robin cursor. A zero retention disables the whole sweep and leaves the staging-metadata sweep untouched.

Claude's agent-to-user file surfacing maps to canonical `file-artifact` messages through one mapper shared by observe and resume: a `SendUserFile` attachment becomes one artifact per file with the basename as its name and the attachment's own media type as its mime, inlined as a `data:` URL when the bytes are readable and emitted header-only when they are not, and it carries `proactive` because the agent SENT it — whatever the native record's status field says, since a file the user asked for is still a file the agent handed over. Inline base64 image blocks become artifacts in user AND assistant messages, reusing the block's own base64 rather than re-encoding, and the user-message row still reports its image count. Artifact paths are stable across a re-map, so history replay dedupes rather than duplicating.

The artifact store keeps its index truthful when the disk does not: a failed atomic persist rolls the in-memory index back rather than leaving a half-written store, every persistence outcome is reported to the health callback, a health callback that throws cannot break the write path, and a corrupt index on load is backed up and reported instead of silently discarded.

The session workspace file API is read-only, bounded, and confined to the session's own directory: list, stat, read, and download refuse traversal, symlinked escapes, and a directory read as a file with 400, an unknown session with 404, and an unauthenticated caller with 401; a read past the configured cap comes back explicitly truncated and a download past its own cap is refused with 413; range requests answer the closed, open, suffix, and If-Range forms exactly and 416 outside them; an absolute or `~` path is normalized to the workspace-relative form when it resolves inside and refused when it does not. Every HTTP client is treated as remote, so the whole surface is default-denied with 403 until the host's filesystem feature is explicitly enabled.
